world.title: ACWECA: Webinar Charts New Paths for Evangelization in The Digital Frontier
world.description:
Sr Teresa Banda
In a world where digital platforms are shaping how people connect, communicate, and search for meaning, the Church is increasingly called to be present where life unfolds, including in the digital space. For consecrated religious men and women, this presents not only a challenge but also a profound opportunity to witness, evangelize, and accompany others in new and meaningful ways.
On 28th April 2026, the Association of Consecrated Women in Eastern and Central Africa (ACWECA) successfully hosted a transformative virtual session that brought together over 300 religious men and women from Eastern and Central Africa. The session focused on empowering consecrated women to embrace the digital environment as a vital space for mission, witness, and evangelization in today’s rapidly evolving world.
This timely initiative responded to the call of the Synod on Synodality, which recognizes digital culture not merely as a tool, but as an essential dimension of the Church’s mission in the contemporary world (Final Document no. 59). The gathering created a dynamic platform for reflection, learning and sharing, aimed at strengthening the capacity of consecrated women to engage confidently and purposefully in digital evangelization while upholding their dignity, promoting the mission of the Church and embodying the synodal spirit of communion, participation and mission.
The webinar was graced by the keynote address of Rev. Fr. Andrew Kaufa (SMM), AMECEA Social Communication Coordinator, who offered profound insights into the Church’s growing presence in the digital space. He emphasized the need for intentional, ethical, and creative engagement online, encouraging consecrated women to see digital platforms as fertile ground for evangelization and pastoral outreach. He also highlighted the importance of investing in clear communication strategies and policies to enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of communication among religious communities.
A rich panel discussion further deepened the conversation, divided into two key parts. The first part featured religious congregation leadership and communication experts who shared reflections on digital evangelization and the mission of consecrated women. Sr. Mother Felicita Humwara, Superior General of the Sisters of the Sacred Heart of Jesus (SHS) from South Sudan, highlighted the importance of leadership support in fostering digital engagement within congregations. Sr. Michelle Njeri, a member of the Franciscan Sisters of the Immaculate Conception (OSF) and part of the Communication Network for Catholic Sisters (CNCS) in Kenya, brought practical perspectives on communication strategies and the effective use of digital tools in ministry.
The second part of the panel focused on lived experiences from the field, where panelists shared testimonies, best practices, and recommendations drawn from their digital mission journeys. Rev. Sr. Veronica Masikinye, Superior General of the Little Children of Our Blessed Lady (LCBL) in Zimbabwe, reflected on formation and mentorship in nurturing digitally aware religious. Sr. Immaculate Banda, a young sister from the Daughters of Mary Theresa of Ledóchowska (DMTL) in Malawi, offered an inspiring voice of the younger generation, highlighting the importance of authenticity, creativity, and courage in engaging online audiences.
The interactive session that followed created a vibrant space of dialogue, where participants shared experiences, asked thoughtful questions, and deepened mutual learning. This exchange reflected the beauty of synodality, listening, and walking together in a spirit of unity and a common mission.
The webinar concluded with a strong call to embrace the digital space as a true missionary territory, not merely a communication tool. It emphasized the need for a consistent and authentic digital presence, strengthened through ongoing capacity building and deeper collaboration among congregations. Consecrated women are invited to evangelize, accompany, and witness to the Gospel in this space, especially among young people, while ensuring inclusivity by supporting young sisters and those with limited access to technology so that no one is left behind. The digital world is not separate from mission; it is part of it, calling for a presence rooted in authentic Gospel witness, responsible engagement, and a commitment to communion and participation.
The conversation further underscored the importance of walking together across generations, where the wisdom of older sisters and the digital creativity of younger ones enrich the mission in diverse contexts. At the heart of this journey is authentic witness living the Gospel with simplicity and integrity so that others may encounter Christ. The need for intentional formation in digital mission, including communication skills, online safety, and ethical engagement, was strongly affirmed. While technology offers great opportunities, it must always serve genuine human relationships. Moving forward, the Church is called to deepen collaboration, foster meaningful connections, and develop clear policies and guiding frameworks to ensure that digital evangelization remains safe, inclusive, and truly life-giving, a shared “tent of encounter” where all are welcomed and valued.
